subject: Strength of Materials
summary: the elastic curve equation, standard cases, superposition, Macaulay's method, moment-area theorems and propped cantilevers
next_day: Strength of Materials, Torsion, Thin Cylinders & Springs

questions.text: The differential equation of the elastic curve of a beam (small deflections, y upward, sagging moment positive) is
solution: Concept: Curvature 1/R = M/(EI), and for small slopes 1/R ≈ d²y/dx².
So EI y'' = M; differentiating, EI y''' = V and EI y'''' = −w (load intensity).
Exam tip: Integrate M once for slope, twice for deflection; fix the two constants from the supports.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a 20 kN point load at midspan. With EI = 10000 kN·m², the maximum deflection (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Central point load on a simply supported beam: δmax = PL³/(48EI) at midspan.
Exam tip: kN and kN·m² give metres directly; multiply by 1000 for mm.

questions.text: The slope at each support of a simply supported beam of span L carrying a UDL w over the whole span is
solution: Concept: By symmetry the slope is zero at midspan; θA = area of M/EI diagram from A to midspan.
Area of half the parabola = (2/3) × (L/2) × (wL²/8) = wL³/24 → θA = wL³/(24EI)
Exam tip: Central point load gives θA = PL²/(16EI).

questions.text: The cantilever AB shown (fixed at A, length 3 m, EI = 9000 kN·m²) carries a UDL of 2 kN/m over its whole length and a 5 kN load at the free end B. The deflection of B (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Superposition: add the deflections due to each load acting alone (linear elastic beam).
Exam tip: Memorise the 4 basic cantilever and 4 basic SS-beam cases; most GATE deflection questions are superpositions of them.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of rectangular section carries a central load. If the depth of the section is doubled (width unchanged), the maximum deflection becomes
solution: Concept: δ ∝ 1/I and I = bd³/12 ∝ d³.
Doubling d multiplies I by 8 → deflection becomes 1/8.
Bending stress (∝ 1/d²) would fall to 1/4.
Exam tip: Depth is the cheapest way to stiffen a beam.

questions.text: The simply supported beam AB shown (span 6 m, EI = 30000 kN·m²) carries 20 kN loads at 2 m from each support. The deflection at midspan (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept (Macaulay): RA = RB = 20 kN. EI y'' = 20x − 20⟨x − 2⟩ − 20⟨x − 4⟩.
EI y = (20/6)x³ − (20/6)⟨x − 2⟩³ − (20/6)⟨x − 4⟩³ + C<sub>1</sub>x; y(0) = 0 gives C<sub>2</sub> = 0, and y(6) = 0 gives C<sub>1</sub> = −80.
Exam tip: Terms in Macaulay brackets are dropped whenever the bracket is negative.

questions.text: By the second moment-area theorem, the vertical distance of a point B on the elastic curve from the tangent drawn at point A equals
opts: the moment, about B, of the M/EI diagram area between A and B
the area of the M/EI diagram between A and B
the moment, about A, of the M/EI diagram area between A and B
the slope at B multiplied by AB
questions.ans: (A) the moment, about B, of the M/EI diagram area between A and B
solution: Concept: tB/A = ∫ (M/EI) x̄B dx from A to B, with distances measured from B (the point whose deviation is wanted).
Taking moments about A instead gives t<sub>A/B</sub>, the deviation of A from the tangent at B.
Exam tip: For a cantilever, take the tangent at the fixed end (it is horizontal), so tB/A is the deflection itself.

questions.text: A cantilever 2 m long (EI = 5000 kN·m²) carries a clockwise couple of 10 kN·m at its free end. The deflection of the free end (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: An end couple gives a constant bending moment M0 over the whole length.
Exam tip: The elastic curve under constant M is a circular arc of radius R = EI/M0.

questions.text: A propped cantilever of span L (fixed at A, propped at B) carries a point load P at midspan. The reaction at the prop is
solution: Concept: Compatibility: the prop deflection is zero.
Without the prop, the free end deflects 5PL³/(48EI) (load at mid-length). The prop force R lifts it by RL³/(3EI).
RL³/3EI = 5PL³/48EI → R = 5P/16; the fixed end takes 11P/16.
Exam tip: 3wL/8 is the prop reaction for a UDL. Do not mix the two.

questions.text: The overhanging beam ABC shown (span AB = 4 m, overhang BC = 1 m, EI = 10000 kN·m²) carries a 10 kN load at the free end C. The downward deflection of C (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: δC = (deflection of BC as a cantilever) + (rotation of the span at B) × BC.
The moment at B is Pa = 10 kN·m; it rotates the simply supported span at B by θ<sub>B</sub> = (Pa)L/(3EI) = 10 × 4/30000 = 0.001333 rad.
Cantilever part: Pa³/(3EI) = 10 × 1/30000 = 0.000333 m; rotation part: θ<sub>B</sub> × a = 0.001333 m
δC = 0.000333 + 0.001333 = 0.001667 m = 1.67 mm ↓ = Pa²(L + a)/(3EI). The span AB bows upward (max 1.03 mm).
Exam tip: In overhang problems, never forget the rotation at the support carried to the tip.

questions.text: For a beam of span L carrying a UDL over the whole span, the ratio of the maximum deflection with both ends fixed to that with both ends simply supported is
solution: Concept: Fixed-fixed: wL⁴/(384EI). Simply supported: 5wL⁴/(384EI).
Ratio = 1/5.
Exam tip: For a central point load the same ratio is 1/4 (PL³/192EI vs PL³/48EI).

questions.text: A cantilever of length L carries a point load at its free end. The deflection at the mid-length, as a fraction of the free-end deflection, is ______ (round off to four decimal places)
solution: Concept: For an end load, y(x) = Px²(3L − x)/(6EI), x from the fixed end.
Exam tip: By Maxwell's reciprocal theorem, 5PL³/48EI is also the free-end deflection for a load at mid-length.

questions.text: A beam is bent by equal and opposite couples at its ends (pure bending). Its elastic curve is
solution: Concept: 1/R = M/(EI); with M constant along the beam, the curvature is constant.
Constant curvature means a circular arc. The small-slope equation y'' = M/EI gives a parabola, which is the same arc to first order.
Exam tip: A UDL gives a quartic curve and a point load a cubic between loads.

questions.text: A simply supported floor beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. With E = 200 GPa and a deflection limit of span/360, the minimum second moment of area required is ______ × 10⁶ mm⁴
solution: Concept: Serviceability: 5wL⁴/(384EI) ≤ L/360.
Exam tip: 1 m⁴ = 10¹² mm⁴; unit slips here cost marks.

questions.text: Two simply supported beams are identical except that the second has twice the span. Each carries the same central point load. Compared with the first, the second beam has
opts: 2 times the maximum bending stress and 8 times the maximum deflection
2 times the stress and 4 times the deflection
4 times the stress and 8 times the deflection
the same stress and 8 times the deflection
questions.ans: (A) 2 times the maximum bending stress and 8 times the maximum deflection
solution: Concept: Mmax = PL/4 ∝ L, so σ ∝ L; δ = PL³/(48EI) ∝ L³.
Doubling L: σ × 2, δ × 8 → (A).
Exam tip: Long spans are usually limited by deflection, short spans by strength.
